sections.h2: What does a Polk County seller need to know about the county?
sections.html:
Polk County is the busiest of the four Georgia counties in the Census Bureau's comparison table, with 45,514 residents on its July 2025 estimate. The 2010 census found 41,475, and the 2020 census found 42,853. Cedartown and Rockmart each host a tax commissioner office.

Land area is 310.34 square miles, with 138.1 residents per square mile in 2020, the densest of the group. The mean commute is 30.5 minutes. The county's 2023 payroll reached $479,368,000 across 670 employer establishments, and those employers counted 10,640 jobs. Health care and social assistance took in $101,139,000 in 2022, and hotels and restaurants sold $80,215,000.

Retail sales of $538,472,000 in 2022 work out to $12,331 per resident. Another 3,187 businesses have no employees at all, so a share of Polk sellers are self-employed owners who may also hold commercial space or equipment on the tax rolls.

sections.h2: How do Polk County homes compare on price and ownership?
sections.html:
Polk is the lowest-priced county of the four. The middle value of a home that its owner occupies is $187,600, and owners live in only 66.0% of housing.

Median household income is $58,515 and per person income is $28,773. Owners with a mortgage report $1,428 in monthly costs, and owners without one report $502. With one in three homes occupied by someone other than the owner, a landlord selling a rental should expect questions about leases and tenant access.

sections.h2: What do Polk County's jobs and household numbers suggest for sellers?
sections.html:
Employment at Polk employers grew 2.0% between 2022 and 2023, a slower pace than the other three counties managed. Transportation and warehousing receipts reached $51,678,000 in 2022, which hints at logistics work near the county's roads and rail lines. The labor force takes in 58.1% of residents over 16.

Households average 2.72 people, and 89.8% of residents lived at the same address a year earlier. Population is up 6.2% since the 2020 base, while the county issued 217 building permits last year, so supply of new homes is thin next to the 17,654 existing units. Computer access is 93.5% of households.

For a seller, the takeaway is that the buyer pool is local and budget-conscious. A house that arrives at the table with its tax paid and a clear title is easier to finance, and lenders and title companies check for a recorded FIFA before they fund a loan.

The county is mixed in age and background. Children under 18 are 24.6% of residents and people 65 and older are 17.9%. About 80.1% identify as White alone, 12.7% as Black alone and 15.1% as Hispanic or Latino, and 6.1% were born outside the United States. A language other than English is spoken at home by 12.1% of residents aged 5 and over.

Education runs below the other three counties: 84.5% of adults hold a high school diploma and 15.4% hold a bachelor's degree. A 12.5% disability rate under age 65 and a 16.3% uninsured rate round out the picture. Broadband reaches 87.4% of households, and 1,810 residents are veterans.

Pricing a home for this market means leaning on nearby sales and keeping the closing simple, since many buyers rely on a mortgage and a clean title.

sections.h2: Where are the Polk County tax offices?
sections.html:
There are two counters, both open weekdays from 9 am to 5 pm and shut for lunch from 12:45 to 2:00.

  • Cedartown: 144 West Ave, GA 30125.
  • Rockmart: 316 N Piedmont Ave, GA 30153.
  • Shared contact: (770) 749-2125 or taxoffice@polkga.org.
  • Assessors: (770) 749-2108.

The tax commissioner's page says the county does not bill city tax. Each city sends its own, so a Rockmart or Cedartown seller may need a payoff from the city clerk in addition to the county. The county also says it does not sell tax liens.

sections.h2: When does a Polk County bill become late?
sections.html:
That depends on which county page you read, so confirm the date on your bill. The tax commissioner FAQ says December 20 is normal, and the county tax commissioner page says taxes fall due sixty days after the bill is mailed.

The FAQ lays out the cost of lateness this way: 1% interest each month once the date passes, then a 10% penalty on anything still open after 90 days. A homestead parcel owing under $500 skips that penalty. Once 90 days pass, the tax office may record a FIFA at the Clerk of Superior Court. The record is open to the public, which the FAQ warns can show up in credit reports.

A bill is mailed to the owner and not to a lender. If a mortgage company escrows your tax, forward the bill to the servicer and include your loan number.

sections.h2: What happened with Polk County's 2026 assessment notices?
sections.html:
The Board of Assessors mailed them on July 17, 2026. Each notice starts a 45-day appeal clock, so owners who did not respond within that time have passed the deadline for the 2026 values.

The county directs owners to qpublic.net/ga/polk to see property characteristics, ownership, assessed values, parcel maps and sales history. Its tax estimator asks you to choose the right tax district, choose Not Exempt, key in the market value on the notice, and then subtract the estimated tax savings printed on the notice. The county describes the result as an estimate only, because final millage rates may differ.

An appeal goes to the assessors first. A dispute that stays open can move on to the Grand Jury's appointed Board of Equalization or to an arbitrator, with a superior court filing available after that.

sections.h2: Which exemptions can a Polk County owner claim?
sections.html:
Four conditions apply: you owned the property on January 1, it is your legal residence, you live in it, and you claim no other homestead anywhere. Filing is open all year, but the paperwork has to arrive before April 1 to affect that year's bill.

  • First $2,000 of assessed value off county, state and school tax for a homestead.
  • Age 65: $20,000 off school tax and $4,000 off county tax.
  • Age 62 with owner and spouse income under $10,000: extra relief.
  • Age 70 with household income under $10,000: extra relief.
  • Veterans who are 100% permanently disabled: an added exemption.

Only your primary home can be homesteaded, and a move means a fresh application.

sections.h2: How do I close a Polk County sale when tax is owed?
sections.html:
Get the numbers first and pay them from the sale proceeds. Polk's commissioner says tax liens are not sold, but a recorded FIFA still clouds the title until it is satisfied.

  1. Phone (770) 749-2125 for the balance, with interest and penalty.
  2. Ask if a FIFA is on file.
  3. Request a city payoff when the house sits inside city limits.
  4. Put each amount on the settlement statement.

If a tenant, a repair list or an inherited deed is slowing a standard listing, an as-is buyer can work around them and settle the tax at closing.

faqs.q: What is the Polk County due date for tax?
faqs.a: The bill itself controls. The FAQ names December 20, and the county's commissioner page says sixty days after the mailing date.

faqs.q: How much interest does Polk County charge?
faqs.a: The FAQ sets 1% a month in interest starting after the due date and a 10% penalty at the 90-day mark.

faqs.q: Where do Polk County residents pay tax in person?
faqs.a: At 144 West Ave in Cedartown or 316 N Piedmont Ave in Rockmart, on weekdays from 9 am to 5 pm.

faqs.q: Is the 2026 Polk County appeal period still open?
faqs.a: No. No. The 2026 notices went out July 17, 2026, and owners had 45 days from that date.

faqs.q: Does Polk County bill city tax too?
faqs.a: No. Cities within Polk send their own bills, so request that balance from the city clerk before the closing date.
